title: Operator Mosaic: federated tasklet orchestrator for admin automation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a lightweight, federated tasklet orchestrator (codename: Operator Mosaic) that treats runbooks as composable, idempotent tasks to power admin utilities and support automation. Goal: enable on-call and support agents to invoke deterministic sequences (ad hoc or scheduled) with operator-level RBAC, audit trails, and safe rollback/cutover semantics. This ticket covers the core coordinator + admission controls and the initial operator UX surface for canarying taskflows.
comments: 2025-01-22 - Ava Martinez: Kickoff meeting summary attached to Confluence. Agreed scope: coordinator core, tasklet registry, admission layer, audit hooks, basic web UI. Decided to keep tasklet implementations language-agnostic (HTTP/gRPC shim) to ease adoption.

2025-01-28 - Liam Chen: Prototype of coordinator completed. Uses gRPC for control plane (chosen for streaming + metadata propagation). Added optimistic locking on task metadata to reduce KV churn. Initial unit tests added; integration tests failing around concurrent cache eviction (race condition in KV cache driver).

2025-01-30 - Priya Nair (Security): Reviewed threat model. Recommendations: require `run_as` tokens for privileged tasklets, enforce KMS-wrapped credentials per-tenant, and record full deterministic inputs for replayability. Marked security_review_required = true.

2025-02-02 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Load test notes: coordinator saturates at 350 reqs/s under 16ms median latency when tasklet execution is mocked; real tasklets with disk I/O push latency to 120ms p50. SRE suggests adding soft concurrency limits per-tasklet and circuit-breaker for noisy neighbors.

2025-02-04 - Liam Chen: Design decision log: split admission layer into two phases: (1) policy validation and RBAC check, (2) runtime admission with capacity check and cost-accounting. Trade-off: two-phase check increases control-plane overhead but prevents dangerous long-running tasks from starting during incidents.

2025-02-05 - Ava Martinez: PR #42 opened for coordinator API and tasklet registry. Needs UX/PM review for operator console integration. Follow-ups: create canary plan, add end-to-end test harness, and implement per-tenant audit export.

2025-02-06 - Liam Chen: Blockers: flaky integration tests caused by transient KV lock timeouts (investigating). Next steps for this sprint: fix KV driver backoff, add per-tasklet throttles, and wire audit events to event-sink. Planned canary rollout to internal ops namespace after tests pass.
2025-02-06 - Product feedback (Priya Nair): PM asks for a simple 'dry-run' mode for runbooks-as-tasks so support can simulate effects without committing changes. Added as follow-up sub-issue.
next_steps: Stabilize KV driver backoff and eliminate integration flakiness
Implement per-tasklet soft concurrency limits and circuit-breaker
Add dry-run mode and UX toggle on operator console
Complete security gating (KMS integration) and audit exports
Plan internal canary: ops-internal namespace -> limited customers
